assessments.reasoning: Seven contiguous parts cover the 101,590-byte SPDX json/details record at the claimed commit, with reported SHA-256 c26841db6b15d7b020d9e74412ce104e5cff445ebcb27b4c2ee91bf8ebb1d593. Part 1 gives isDeprecatedLicenseId=false. Part 4 gives licenseId=LGPL-2.1-only, the name, comments and only header. Its seeAlso entries cite GNU’s standalone and regular LGPL-2.1 HTML pages and OSI’s LGPL-2.1-only page. These are references within the record. They were not separately acquired as corroboration.

The GitHub API object for the SPDX license-list-data repository identifies annotated tag 76c9a79bb7d2bf851143b76b3935a4d7cbaa644b as v3.29.0. Its target has type commit and SHA 31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48, matching the JSON locator. GitHub reports the tag as unsigned. The evidence establishes the repository’s tag target without signer verification.

The complete GNU text at the claimed digest supplies edition and notice context. Section 0 identifies the copyright holder or other authorized party as the source of the notice. Section 13 distinguishes a numbered version with a later-version option from an unnumbered grant. The application example expressly offers later versions. SPDX supplies the positive evidence for the only header and identifier.

limitations: “Alone” paraphrases the version election. The SPDX header does not require the literal word “only.” The claim’s “granting use” summarizes a header that specifically addresses redistribution and modification.

The notice condition appears in the statement while conditions is empty and the edition scope is shared with the or-later record. The SPDX key preserves the distinction, but an export that drops the statement and treats the bare edition as sufficient would lose it.
This finding covers an SPDX license-list entry at the pinned release. An actual file’s applicable notice and modifications require their own evidence.
reasoning: SPDX 3.29.0 lists LGPL-2.1-only for the version-2.1-alone election. Its standard header ends the version clause at “version 2.1.” Its comments explicitly distinguish LGPL-2.1-or-later. The apparent inconsistency is that the same record’s full license text includes the publisher’s or-later example. The claim is accurate for a notice that actually limits the grant to 2.1. It would be inaccurate to describe the pinned FSF example itself as an only notice.
